candidates: In a `"type": "module"` package, do not add `"main"` or `"require"` export fields that point to `.js` UMD/bundled files in the same directory as ESM files — Node.js treats all `.js` files in that directory as ESM, so `require()` on those files will fail at runtime. If CJS support is genuinely required alongside a UMD bundle, use `.cjs` file extensions or place the CJS files in a subdirectory with its own `{ "type": "commonjs" }` package.json. Treat CJS wiring in package.json as a separate concern from adding a UMD/IIFE build output, and handle it in a separate PR.

When modifying `exports`, `types`, or `main` fields in package.json, verify that type exports are correct for all relevant `moduleResolution` modes using https://arethetypeswrong.github.io before merging, to catch CJS/ESM TypeScript incompatibilities (e.g. broken types under `moduleResolution: node16`).

When removing or renaming files in the `dist/` directory of a published npm package, check whether those paths are referenced by CDN URLs. `unpkg.com` returns a 404 for missing files (unlike jsdelivr, which falls back to older versions), permanently breaking all `<script src>` CDN links for downstream consumers. The `dist/mermaid.min.js` filename in particular has a large number of CDN dependents and must be treated as a stable public artifact that should not be removed.
